## 2026-04-14 — INCIDENT: Config clobber / OpenClaw down ~1hr

- **Quality:** N/A (infrastructure failure, not a session) | **Initiative:** 1/5
- **What happened:** Latch wrote a partial config object to `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` — likely via a config.set API call containing only `{ acp: { defaultAgent: 'latch' } }`. OpenClaw's config API accepted it as a full document replace, stripping all other top-level keys: `gateway`, `models`, `agents`, `channels`, `commands`, `meta`, `wizard`. On restart, OpenClaw's startup guard detected missing `gateway.mode` and blocked start, entering an auth retry loop. Gateway was down from 11:16am until diagnosed and restored via `.bak` file.
- **Root cause:** Direct/partial config write without read-merge-write pattern.
- **Lesson:** **NEVER write to `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` directly or via any API that does a full document replace.** Always use the safe wrapper: `/Users/black/aaron-context/scripts/openclaw_config_set.py <key.path> <value>`. This script reads the full config, merges the single key, validates required keys are still present, then writes. Direct writes, even of valid values, will clobber the entire config on API calls that don't merge.
- **Required keys that must always be present:** `meta`, `wizard`, `acp`, `models`, `agents`, `channels`, `gateway`, `plugins`. If any are missing, OpenClaw will not start.
- **Recovery path (if this happens again):** `cp ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.bak ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` then set any intentional changes via `openclaw_config_set.py`, then `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/ai.openclaw.gateway`.
- **Trigger idea:** Perception trigger on `openclaw.json` writes — if file size drops below 2KB or key count drops below 8, fire alert and abort.
